info.name: PotchMatch Demo Flow
info.description:
Pre-built requests for the ITRI623 Deliverable 1 demo video: register a coach, set up their profile and a coaching session, then register a player, fail on insufficient funds, add funds, and succeed. Run top to bottom inside each folder - Login requests capture the JWT into {{authToken}} automatically, and Create Coaching Session captures {{bookingId}} automatically, so nothing needs to be copy-pasted by hand during the recording.

Before recording: bump the scheduledAt date in 'Create Coaching Session' if you end up recording after 7 September 2026 (the backend rejects any date that isn't in the future).

request.description: isCoach must be true here - that's what unlocks the coaching-session option later. Club is PCC (Potchefstroom Country Club).

body.raw:
{
  "name": "Wickus",
  "surname": "van Niekerk",
  "email": "wickusvn@gmail.com",
  "clubId": "pcc",
  "rank": "Unranked",
  "coachBio": "Level 2 SA Squash-certified coach with 8 years of experience developing club and provincial players. Focused on movement efficiency, shot accuracy, and match-day mental preparation.",
  "coachingLevel": "SA Squash Level 2 Coach",
  "hourlyRateZAR": 100
}

request.description: rank is just echoed back unchanged (it's not editable here) - 'Unranked' matches what a brand-new player is seeded with.
IMPORTANT: scheduledAt must be a future date/time - if you're recording after 7 September 2026, bump this date first or the backend will 400 it.
Club is 'defence' (Potchefstroom Defence Squash Club) - a different club to the coach's, which is fine: coaching sessions and challenges are visible/joinable across clubs on the map.
A brand-new wallet always starts at R0 - this is here just to show that on screen before the accept attempt below fails.

item.name: Accept Coaching Session - expect 402 Insufficient Funds

request.description: This is expected to fail with 402 - the player's wallet is still R0. That's the deliberate business-rule rejection, not a bug (see BookingController.Accept -> PaymentService /api/payments/hold).

exec: pm.test('Insufficient funds (402) - this is expected!', () => pm.response.to.have.status(402));

request.description: This is the same demo top-up flow as the Dashboard's 'Add Funds' modal - no real card is charged either way.

Now that the wallet has R200, this should succeed - watch the UI's dashboard update too, and check the booking-service/payment-service logs for the CorrelationId linking this one request across both services.

item.name: Phase 2 — SOC
item.description: Cycle A SOC pipeline demo. Run top to bottom: log in as admin, send 'Failed Login x1' five times, wait ~15 s, then list/inspect alerts. Needs the seeded admin (admin@potchmatch.local). The final request needs a player token in {{authToken}}.

request.description: Seeded admin account. Stores the JWT in {{adminToken}} (separate from {{authToken}} so player logins do not overwrite it).

Click Send 5 times (do not use the Runner: it would re-run the whole folder) to trigger the 'Multiple Failed Logins' rule (5 failures in 5 minutes for one account). Rule 1 raises TWO alerts for the same failed logins: one for the account and one for the source IP. Sending 3 more later should add to the same alerts.
Wait ~15 s after the failed logins (the rule engine runs every 15 s). Stores the id of the first Multiple Failed Logins alert as {{alertId}} (Rule 1 raises two: account and IP).

exec: const login = Array.isArray(alerts) ? alerts.find(a => a.ruleName === 'Multiple Failed Logins') : undefined;
pm.test('An open Multiple Failed Logins alert exists', () => pm.expect(login, 'no open Multiple Failed Logins alert yet').to.exist);
pm.test('Rule is Multiple Failed Logins', () => pm.expect(alert.ruleName).to.eql('Multiple Failed Logins'));

request.description: Uses {{authToken}}, which is the player's JWT after running 'Login Player' in folder 2 (register the player first if needed).

item.name: Phase 2 — RAG
item.description: Cycle C GraphRAG assistant, admin only. Run the 'Phase 2 — SOC' folder first (failed logins), wait ~45 s for the graph sync, then run this folder top to bottom. Ask requests need a Gemini API key on the rag-service (otherwise 503 rag_disabled). The Rule 5 probe needs the folder 2 player registered.

Returns { enabled, model, reason }. enabled is false when no Gemini API key is configured; the ask requests then return 503 rag_disabled.

exec: pm.test('status has enabled + model', () => { pm.expect(s).to.have.property('enabled'); pm.expect(s).to.have.property('model'); });

item.name: Rule 5 probe: wait, then list alerts

request.description: Wait ~30 s after the three 403s (SOC detection runs every 15 s), then send this. Asserts a GRAPH_ACCESS alert exists.
